_meta.purpose: Regression fixture for the harness-coverage metric. Detects drift in scripts/harness-coverage.py output shape, cell-id enumeration, intentional-gap annotation, 60% threshold application, and the meaningful/trivial fire split. Per Bockeler L476, the journal is hand-curated (not agent-generated) to avoid the 'AI-generated tests are not good enough yet' failure mode.

pedagogical_arc.s01_s08_fresh_install: 8 sessions in the pre-prev window; the harness exists but no journal events are emitted. The script filters these out (before now-60d).
pedagogical_arc.s09_s15_early_firing: 7 sessions dated 2026-03-19 to 2026-04-12 (T09:00:00.000Z). The script's prev window starts at runtime-relative now-60d, which for an eval run on 2026-06-15T17:08 is 2026-04-16T17:08. None of the s09-s15 sessions fall in the prev window because their 09:00 UTC timestamp is before 17:08 UTC on 2026-04-16. They are dropped from both the current and prev windows by the script's _stream_journal filter (they land in the earlier-ignored bucket). This is the wall-clock dependency captured in the note above.
pedagogical_arc.s16_s23_mature_firing: 8 sessions in the prev window; all 4 directions fire. inf-fb is trivial (top_finding=null). This is the 'mid-window stability' phase.
pedagogical_arc.s24_s27_degraded_firing: 4 sessions in the current window; comp-fb (post-edit-audit) goes silent. inf-fb is meaningful again. This is the 'recent degradation starts' phase.
pedagogical_arc.s28_s30_deeply_degraded: 3 sessions in the current window; inf-fb also goes silent. Only comp-ff + inf-ff still fire. This is the 'silent sensor cluster' phase.
pedagogical_arc.s17_s23_mature_firing: 7 sessions dated 2026-04-20 to 2026-05-14 (T09:00:00.000Z). These ARE in the prev window [2026-04-16T17:08, 2026-05-16T17:08) because their 09:00 UTC timestamp is after 17:08 UTC on 2026-04-16. All 7 are tagged 'mature_firing' with all 4 directions firing, but only the inf-fb verdicts are non-trivial because the script's _aggregate_journal applies the event to all inf-fb cells (including inf-fb-behaviour) regardless of the cell's intentional_gap override — the override zeroes population/activation/score but the events still flow into the activation counters.
pedagogical_arc.s16_s23_actual_prev_split: Only s17-s23 (7 sessions, not all 8 of s16-s23) fall in the prev window for an eval run on 2026-06-15T17:08. s16 (2026-04-16T09:00:00.000Z) is BEFORE the prev window's 17:08 cut-off and is dropped. This is the wall-clock quirk that the dry-run revealed and the expected_grid now reflects.

_meta.coverage_hole_note: The metric's 4 status states (populated, stale, intentional_gap, coverage_hole) reduce to 3 in this fixture. coverage_hole requires a direction with zero listed sensors (per design doc section 3.3); the mock registry covers all 4 directions, so no cell lands in coverage_hole. Adding a 4th intentional_gap (e.g. inf-ff-arch-fit per the design doc's 3 known gaps) would require a script-side update to KNOWN_INTENTIONAL_GAPS, which is out of scope for FIX-1 (the brief specifies exactly 1 intentional_gap cell). The 3-state coverage (populated, stale, intentional_gap) is what the metric's design naturally produces for a real harness that lists sensors in all 4 directions.
_meta.score_quirk_note: The comp-ff / comp-fb / inf-ff cells all have cell_score_pct=0 in this fixture, because the script's weighted_score formula (section 3.2) only counts inferential_structural_verdict events toward the meaningful/trivial split. Non-verdict cells (comp-ff PreToolUse gates, comp-fb PostToolUse audits, inf-ff SessionStart doctrine injection) carry hook_fired events with no top_finding, so weighted_score=0 and the cell_score_pct collapses. This is a deterministic property of the current metric design (the 70/30 split is the Q&A #11 anti-gaming mechanism) and is captured here as a regression anchor. If a future revision of the metric changes the weighted_score formula, this fixture's comp-ff / comp-fb / inf-ff cell_score_pct values will shift and the regression will surface the change.
_meta.wall_clock_dependency: The script's rolling window is wall-clock-relative: now-30d, now-60d, computed at script runtime (not at fixture authoring time). The fixture's session timestamps are at T09:00:00.000Z (09:00 UTC). For an eval run on 2026-06-15T17:08:   - current window: [2026-05-16T17:08, 2026-06-15T17:08) = s24-s30 (7 sessions, all after the cut-off)   - prev window:    [2026-04-16T17:08, 2026-05-16T17:08) = s17-s23 (7 sessions after the cut-off)   - earlier (ignored): s01-s16 (16 sessions, all before the prev cut-off) The expected_grid values were derived by dry-running scripts/harness-coverage.py against the fixture's events with a runtime of 2026-06-15T17:08. If the eval is run at a different wall-clock time, the prev/current split shifts. Wave 5 / INT-1 must add a mock_journal / as-of mechanism to the eval runner so the gate is reproducible across eval-run times. The fixture data is the contract; the runtime wiring is downstream.

intentional_gap.rationale: Bockeler L465-L478 names behaviour-inferential-FB as the article's deepest open problem; kbg's verification-gate, fabrication-verdict-log, and inferential-structural-judge are advisory-only per ADR 0002 L115 (LLM-judge-circularity mitigation).
intentional_gap.revisit_when: When a non-model-class judge (different model family) is available; the autonomy invariant forbids a model-driven gating decision from this cell in the meantime.

cases.description: Sanity: the expected_grid contains all 12 cell_ids from the Cartesian product of 4 directions x 3 axes.
cases.assertion: len(expected_grid) == 12 AND set([c['cell_id'] for c in expected_grid]) == {f'{d}-{a}' for d in ('comp-ff','comp-fb','inf-ff','inf-fb') for a in ('maintainability','arch-fit','behaviour')}

cases.description: The 1 known intentional_gap cell is inf-fb-behaviour (Bockeler L465-L478 + ADR 0002 L115). Guards against the intentional_gap annotation being lost or renamed in a future schema revision.
cases.assertion: exactly 1 cell has status='intentional_gap' AND its cell_id == 'inf-fb-behaviour' AND its intentional_gap object has all 4 required keys: rationale, article_citation, kbg_decision_ref, revisit_when

cases.description: All 11 non-intentional_gap cells have cell_score_pct < 60 in this fixture (the metric is running on a degraded harness state). The 60% threshold surfaces every populated + stale cell as a decay candidate; the 1 intentional_gap is excluded.
cases.assertion: len([c for c in expected_grid if c['status'] != 'intentional_gap' and c['cell_score_pct'] < 60]) == 11

cases.description: Drift math is exercised: inf-fb-maintainability and inf-fb-arch-fit both have current cell_score_pct=9 (4 meaningful fires, 0 trivial, weighted_score=0.7) and prev cell_score_pct=7 (7 trivial fires, 0 meaningful, weighted_score=0.3). Drift = current - prev = 9 - 7 = +2. The drift is non-zero and reflects the real wall-clock-relative prev-vs-current split: the prev window contains 7 sessions of all-trivial fires (s17-s23) while the current window contains 4 sessions of all-meaningful fires (s24-s27). The shift from trivial to meaningful is the only signal the script surfaces, and drift captures it.
cases.assertion: inf-fb-maintainability.cell_score_pct == 9 AND inf-fb-maintainability.drift_vs_prev_window_pct == 2 AND inf-fb-arch-fit.cell_score_pct == 9 AND inf-fb-arch-fit.drift_vs_prev_window_pct == 2

cases.description: Verdict quality (section 3.2): inf-fb-maintainability has 4 meaningful fires, 0 trivial fires in the current window -> weighted_score = (4*0.7 + 0*0.3) / 4 = 0.7. cell_score_pct = round(100 * 4/30 * 0.7) = round(9.333) = 9. This guards the 0.7/0.3 split formula.

The fixture is self-contained: _meta.mock_sensors enumerates 5 sensors (a subset of the real hooks/sensors.json registry). The cells' population.sensors_listed values must match the mock-sensor count for each direction. Wave 5 / INT-1 wires the --sensors-path override so the script reads the mock registry rather than the live one. This guards against drift in the script's cell-enumeration logic.
cases.assertion: len(_meta.mock_sensors) == 5 AND expected_grid[comp-ff-*].population.sensors_listed == 2 (matches 2 mock comp-FF sensors) AND expected_grid[comp-fb-*].population.sensors_listed == 1 (matches 1 mock comp-FB sensor) AND expected_grid[inf-ff-*].population.sensors_listed == 1 (matches 1 mock inf-FF sensor) AND expected_grid[inf-fb-maintainability].population.sensors_listed == 1 AND expected_grid[inf-fb-arch-fit].population.sensors_listed == 1 AND expected_grid[inf-fb-behaviour].population.sensors_listed == 0 (forced by KNOWN_INTENTIONAL_GAPS)

cases.description: The silent-sensor alarm (section 3.3 stale status): comp-fb-maintainability, comp-fb-arch-fit, and comp-fb-behaviour all have sensors_listed=1 (post-edit-audit) but actual_events_in_window=0 (post-edit-audit went silent in s24-s30). The status is 'stale' — not 'populated' and not 'coverage_hole'. This is the L553 'high quality or inadequate detection?' signal.
cases.assertion: len([c for c in expected_grid if c['status'] == 'stale']) == 3 AND all 3 stale cells have direction='comp-fb' AND all 3 stale cells have actual_events_in_window=0 AND all 3 stale cells have sensors_listed=1

cases.description: The intentional_gap annotation has exactly the 4 required sub-fields per design doc section 3.4 (rationale, article_citation, kbg_decision_ref, revisit_when). The values are non-empty strings. article_citation references Bockeler L465-L478; kbg_decision_ref references ADR 0002 L115 — the verbatim text from the script's KNOWN_INTENTIONAL_GAPS table.
cases.assertion: inf-fb-behaviour.intentional_gap has exactly the 4 keys {rationale, article_citation, kbg_decision_ref, revisit_when} AND rationale is a non-empty string AND article_citation == 'L465-L478' AND kbg_decision_ref == 'ADR 0002 L115' AND revisit_when is a non-empty string

cases.description: The synthetic journal exercises both the meaningful and trivial fire paths (section 3.2 weighting). Sessions s09-s15 and s24-s27 carry inferential_structural_verdict events with non-null top_finding (meaningful); sessions s16-s23 carry inferential_structural_verdict events with top_finding=null (trivial). The 70/30 weighting in the expected_grid inf-fb cells depends on this split being preserved by the journal shape.
cases.assertion: len([e for s in sessions for e in s['events'] if e['event_type'] == 'inferential_structural_verdict' and e['fields'].get('top_finding') is not None]) >= 1 AND len([e for s in sessions for e in s['events'] if e['event_type'] == 'inferential_structural_verdict' and e['fields'].get('top_finding') is None]) >= 1

cases.description: Dry-run guard: when the script is run on 2026-06-15 with this fixture's journal, the inf-fb-maintainability and inf-fb-arch-fit cells produce cell_score_pct=9 and drift_vs_prev_window_pct=+2. This anchors the expected_grid to the actual script behavior, not a hand-computed approximation. If the script's window-math changes (e.g. a future revision uses session-count instead of wall-clock), this case's expected values will diverge and the regression will surface the change.
cases.assertion: When scripts/harness-coverage.py is invoked on this fixture with --sensors-path pointing at a registry containing the 5 mock_sensors AND --journal-path pointing at the fixture's flattened event stream AND --window-sessions=30 AND a runtime wall-clock of 2026-06-15T17:08:11Z:   inf-fb-maintainability.cell_score_pct == 9 AND   inf-fb-maintainability.drift_vs_prev_window_pct == 2 AND   inf-fb-arch-fit.cell_score_pct == 9 AND   inf-fb-arch-fit.drift_vs_prev_window_pct == 2
